style_when: scale is the story — a port, a refinery, a data centre hall, a rail yard, a skyline of cranes — and the reader needs to feel how big it is
prompt: 200mm telephoto compression down a cold-storage data hall aisle: tall tape-library archive cabinets stacked in flat overlapping layers, brushed steel and graphite-grey panels with round inspection portholes receding toward a far doorway. On the right third one cabinet stands open, an amber worklight glowing inside its tape slot — the single retrieval in a hall of sealed, dormant deep-archive storage. Hard directional light rakes from the far end of the aisle, deep shadows between rows, crystal-clear air, no haze. Steel blue, charcoal and one safety-yellow floor stripe; polished concrete floor, long cast shadows. Wide 16:9 framing, open cabinet off-centre, breathing room above the cabinet line, no people, no text, fine film grain.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, numbers, watermarks, logos, haze, fog
rationale: The story's protagonist is a storage tier, a facility-scale system, so it belongs in its real environment — the cold archive hall — not a studio sweep. Telephoto compression stacks the sealed cabinet rows into flat layers that read as massed cheap capacity, while the single lit open cabinet carries the governing tension: cheap to store, expensive to open. Rule 6 sanctions long_lens_industry for systemic capacity topics, and it breaks the desk's recent run of cinematic, flatlay, night and collage treatments.
cue: cheap to store and expensive to open
subject: a deep-archive tape-library hall with one sealed storage cabinet opened mid-retrieval
core_thesis: The cheapest backup storage tier bills its real cost at restore time, not at list price: a 365-day minimum storage lock and a 15-hour rehydration clock — not $1 per terabyte-month — decide whether the disaster plan actually works.
core_conflict: Deferral economics: vendors batch restore work behind paying jobs, so teams save pennies per terabyte on storage and borrow against the hour they actually need the bytes back.
composition: telephoto one-point perspective down the archive aisle, sealed cabinet rows stacked left, the single open cabinet holding the right third, generous negative space above the cabinet line
